passed_boundaries: primary was never worse than six-motif static control
zero future-half access, state mutation, tokenizer use, or capacity growth
scientific_claim: Under the frozen six-active real-byte boundary test, error-guided selection preserved exact fixed-capacity state and positive held-out prediction gain across all three demand files, but the weakest file retained only 60% of the full sixteen-motif incremental benefit. Six active motifs therefore fall below the preregistered 70% benefit-retention floor even though the state remains useful and no worse than the six-motif static control.
next_question: Test the seven-active boundary using the identical three demand files and first-half error-guided selection to determine whether the 70% benefit-retention floor lies at seven or eight active motifs.
scope: within-lineage real-byte active-capacity boundary; not fresh-corpus generalization
